_what: How a tidy-up of a person's files works, as DATA read by src/file-tidy.mjs and the Tidy up screen (src/workspace/file-tidy-screen.tsx). The person's own AI suggests a title and/or a folder for each file (propose_file_tidy), naming the results already kept about the file that the suggestion comes from; the person accepts or rejects each; accepted ones are applied as one tidy-up that can be undone. `title_kind` is the result kind an applied title is recorded under (its value is { title }). `grounding` is the check ported from the Mac's recording-evidence.mjs: a word counts when it has at least `min_word_length` letters or digits, is not all digits and is not one of `container_words` (words that name the container or a date, never the subject); words match on their first `stem_length` letters; a title is refused when more than one in `missing_share_denominator` of its counted words is missing from the evidence, and a folder that does not exist yet is refused when its last part has counted words and none is in the evidence. `evidence_chars` caps how much text is read from the cited results. `states` says how each state of a suggestion reads on screen (label and tone); `decidable_states` are the ones the person may still accept or reject; `replaceable_states` are the ones a newer suggestion for the same file replaces. `screen` holds the Tidy up screen's words; `words` are the refusals and answers, in plain words.

screen.title: Tidy up
screen.empty_description: Choose files in Files, then Ask my AI to tidy these. Your AI suggests a title and a folder for each from what is known about it, and they wait here for you.

words.no_file: No file has that name in your files.
words.still_arriving: This file is still uploading. Suggest a tidy-up once it has arrived.
words.nothing_suggested: Suggest a title, a folder, or both.
words.bad_title: A title is one line of text, at most {max} characters.
words.bad_folder: A folder is a path starting with / (such as /Clients/Acme), with no empty or dot parts, at most {max} characters.
words.no_evidence_named: Name the results this suggestion comes from in evidence, such as ["transcript"] or ["summary"].
words.evidence_missing: Nothing of kind {kind} is kept for this file yet. Record it first, or cite what is kept.
words.evidence_empty: The cited results hold no words, so nothing supports a suggestion yet.
words.title_ungrounded: The title is not supported by what is known about the file: {missing} is not mentioned there.
words.folder_ungrounded: The new folder {folder} is not supported by what is known about the file. Use a folder that exists, or one its words name.
words.file_changed: This file was renamed, moved or replaced since this was suggested. Ask for a fresh suggestion.
words.evidence_changed: What is known about this file changed since this was suggested ({kinds}). Ask for a fresh suggestion.
words.name_taken: Another file already has the name {name}.
words.not_decidable: This suggestion was already applied or has changed since. Reload the list.
words.nothing_accepted: Nothing is accepted yet. Accept the suggestions you want first.
words.nothing_to_undo: There is no tidy-up to undo.
words.name_needed: Name the tidy-up in one line of at most {max} characters.
words.undo_changed: This tidy-up cannot be undone because these files changed since: {names}.
words.said_proposed: Suggestions waiting for the person on the Tidy up screen: {proposed}. Refused: {refused}.
words.said_list: Waiting for the person: {review}. Accepted and not applied yet: {accepted}.
words.said_not_applied: Not tidied, because the file or what is known about it changed: {refused}. Ask your AI for fresh suggestions.
words.said_undone: The tidy-up is undone: {changes} files are back as they were.
